scope: Kept each supported same-ID lock-order/release-before-wait decision. Rewrote the choices into concise case-specific competing coordination policies, refreshed the Reason with the selected decision plus decisive conflict, and rebound every wrong-option message to a fresh distractor ID. No new product rule or external guarantee was added.

items.learningObjective: Restore progress by resolving a concrete lock-order cycle or releasing local locks before an external wait.
items.decisiveFact: In A fleet charging coordinator, A reservation worker locks the station before the reservation; an expiry worker locks the reservation before the station. They can wait on each other, and unrelated stations should keep reserving. Which coordination change best restores progress without broadening the blocked scope?
items.nearestAlternative: Keep reserve and expiry in opposite orders; retry the one that times out.
items.identityReason: The same opposing-order or external-wait invariant remains decisive, and owner_preserves_contract still expresses the supported coordination decision. Rewritten distractor meanings receive new IDs.
